sec: Thyrotoxicosis: clinical features and Graves disease

items.q: Match the following thyrotoxic features to their system — 1) Weight loss, heat intolerance 2) Tremor, hyperreflexia 3) Atrial fibrillation 4) Diarrhoea … A) Constitutional B) Neurological C) Cardiovascular D) Gastrointestinal
items.exp: Constitutional (weight loss, heat intolerance), neurological (tremor, hyperreflexia), cardiovascular (AF) and gastrointestinal (diarrhoea) are the four feature groups on the page. (Book p910)

items.q: A 35-year-old woman has weight loss, palpitations, lid lag and a diffuse goitre with bruit. Which diagnosis fits?
items.exp: Diffuse goitre with bruit, ophthalmopathy and young female demographic fits Graves disease. (Book p910)

items.q: Assess these thyrotoxic features: I Sinus tachycardia is the most common rhythm. II Atrial fibrillation occurs in a minority of younger patients.
items.exp: Sinus tachycardia is most common; atrial fibrillation occurs in older patients rather than the young. (Book p910)

items.q: Which is the odd one out — a feature of thyrotoxicosis NOT shared with anxiety?
opts: Suppressed TSH with raised free T4
items.exp: Biochemical suppression of TSH with raised free T4 is specific to thyrotoxicosis; tremor, palpitations and weight loss overlap with anxiety. (Book p910)

items.q: The single most specific clinical sign of Graves disease listed on the page is ___.
items.exp: Infiltrative ophthalmopathy is Graves-specific; sinus tachycardia, tremor and diffuse goitre also occur in other causes. (Book p910)

items.q: Match the following Graves feature — 1) Eye signs 2) Skin signs 3) Skeletal signs … A) Exophthalmos, proptosis B) Pretibial myxoedema C) Thyroid acropachy
items.exp: Graves-specific manifestations include exophthalmos (eye), pretibial myxoedema (skin) and thyroid acropachy (skeletal). (Book p910)

items.q: A patient with Graves disease has non-pitting oedema with peau d'orange over the shins. The diagnosis is:
items.exp: Pretibial myxoedema is a Graves-specific dermopathy producing non-pitting oedema with peau d'orange over the shins. (Book p910)

items.q: Assess Graves extra-thyroidal manifestations: I Thyroid acropachy affects the distal phalanges. II Pretibial myxoedema can occur even after euthyroidism is restored.
items.exp: Acropachy is a clubbing-like change of distal phalanges; dermopathy can persist or even appear after euthyroidism. (Book p910)

items.q: Match the following finding to its likely cause in a thyrotoxic patient — 1) Diffuse goitre with bruit 2) Painful tender thyroid 3) Single hot nodule on scan 4) Multiple hot nodules … A) Graves disease B) Subacute thyroiditis C) Toxic adenoma D) Toxic multinodular goitre
items.exp: Graves shows a diffuse goitre with bruit; subacute thyroiditis is painful and tender; a single hot nodule is a toxic adenoma; multiple hot nodules fit toxic MNG. (Book p910)

items.q: A 50-year-old woman has a long-standing multinodular goitre and new atrial fibrillation with weight loss. The most likely aetiology is:
items.exp: Long-standing MNG degenerating into toxic MNG is the typical aetiology in older women with new AF and weight loss. (Book p910)

items.q: Which extra-thyroidal manifestation is unique to Graves disease among all causes of thyrotoxicosis?
items.exp: Infiltrative ophthalmopathy is Graves-specific; other features occur in any thyrotoxicosis. (Book p910)

items.q: The radioactive iodine uptake scan in Graves disease typically shows ___ uptake.
opts: Focally increased in a single nodule
items.exp: Graves produces diffusely increased uptake; toxic adenoma is focal; toxic MNG is multiple focal; thyroiditis is decreased. (Book p910)

items.q: Assess the page's eye-signs grouping: I Proptosis and chemosis are Graves-specific. II Lid lag and lid retraction can occur in any thyrotoxicosis.
items.exp: Infiltrative eye signs are Graves-specific; lid lag and lid retraction occur in any thyrotoxicosis because of sympathetic overactivity. (Book p910)
